titulo: The sky posts once a night. No notification.
caption:
Confession: some nights the only light we look at is a screen.
When I step outside after dark, I look up once. One breath, eyes up.
Source: US Naval Observatory, full moon 26 October 2026, 04:12 UTC (23:12 Sunday in Colombia). https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/MoonPhases
For the one who always points at the moon.
Not while driving or crossing a street.
The tool is on the page: link in bio.
by NMR
alt: 1: On black, a phone stands plugged in at the left with a small dot on its corner; its cable runs off the right edge. The sky posts once a night. No notification. Seven slides. Keep the last one. 2: The cable keeps running across a deep blue field. Tonight the moon is full. It asks for nothing: no tap, no streak, no reply. 3: The cable passes under a window. The phone lights up, buzzes, keeps score. The sky opens every night and never sends a reminder. 4: The cable ends at a door. When you step outside after dark. 5: The plug lies on the floor; Cella stands outside looking up at a round moon. Look up once. One breath, eyes up. Clouds count too. 6: Cella with eyes closed under the moon. What did you notice first? US Naval Observatory: full moon 26 October, 04:12 UTC, Sunday night in the Americas. 7: A framed card on white, with the moon where the phone's dot was on the first slide. When you step outside after dark: look up once. For the one who always points at the moon. Not while driving or crossing a street.
